## Result and scope
Candidate full negative resolution of problem 30004807 / OWR-8415343-010 after one substantive attempt. The static metric g = -(1-a/rho)^(-2) dt^2 + (1-a/rho)^4 delta has regular negative-mass ZAS slices, but a smooth boundary-reaching radial test gives an absolutely convergent weak Bianchi integral of -8 pi.

The claim concerns the geometric universal conjecture on OWR pp. 2232–2233 under BKTZ Definition 2.1's boundary-reaching test convention. The null energy condition is violated. Stronger BKTZ hypotheses, specified matter models, and collapsed-point/worldline test conventions are excluded. No novelty or historical-priority claim is made.

## Verification
- Six frozen author files preserved byte for byte
- Full independent adversarial AI audit included without abridgment
- All 17 author checks and 35 independent controls pass, including three rejected false alternatives
- Both OWR pages and the boundary-test definitions visually inspected in the independent audit
- All 14 remote files read back exactly; one commit ahead of fresh main
- Only this queue row's status, turns, and previously blank findings cell changed; every other queue byte preserved

See [publication notes](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/97b2ed225574ca61bd03cb8db021a533e04938dc/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30004807/PUBLICATION_NOTES.md), [proof](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/97b2ed225574ca61bd03cb8db021a533e04938dc/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30004807/release/PROOF.md), and [complete audit](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/97b2ed225574ca61bd03cb8db021a533e04938dc/unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30004807/audit/AUDIT_REPORT.md).

This remains a draft with queue status claimed_solved (1/5). The mathematical target is complete within its explicit scope, but this is AI-assisted research and independent AI audit, not human peer review or journal acceptance. No PDF, source corpus, private catalogue material, merge, release, or DOI is included.
title: Counterexample to regular-ZAS weak Bianchi conjecture (30004807)
